nodes.title: Finite p-local spectra
nodes.statement: Let Sp_(p) be spectra whose integer homotopy groups are Z_(p)-modules. Let FinSp_(p) be the idempotent-complete stable subcategory generated by S_(p) under finite sums, shifts and cofibers. Its objects are retracts of p-localizations of finite cell spectra; a finite spectrum here always means this compact stable notion.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Invert the degree-q sphere maps for primes q different from p and use their mapping telescopes.
Take the retract closure of finite sphere-cell constructions. Identify the compact generators with the sphere and its shifts.
acceptance: S_(p) is finite p-local, even though its underlying integral spectrum need not be compact.
S/p lies in FinSp_(p) and multiplication by any q different from p is invertible.
An infinite wedge of nonzero copies of S_(p) is not compact in Sp_(p).

nodes.statement: For a spectrum E, an E-acyclic A satisfies E⊗A≃0; an E-equivalence has E-acyclic cofiber. An E-local Y has contractible Map(A,Y) for every E-acyclic A, equivalently Map(f,Y) is an equivalence for every E-equivalence f. Construct the accessible exact reflector L_E:Sp→Sp_E with unit η, natural initial among maps from X to E-local spectra. Define the Bousfield class ⟨E⟩ by its acyclics, with ⟨E⟩≤⟨F⟩ when every F-acyclic is E-acyclic. Smashing means L_E X≃L_E S⊗X compatibly with η.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use accessibility of tensoring by E and the stable accessible-localization input requested from EDS.
Identify local objects by mapping spaces; the ordinary homotopy-category predicate is compatible with the Mathlib orthogonality convention.
Descend tensor to the local category; joins of Bousfield classes are represented by wedges.

nodes.title: Complex orientations
nodes.statement: A complex orientation of a homotopy commutative ring spectrum E is x∈Ẽ²(CP∞) restricting to 1∈E⁰(*) under CP¹≃S². The projective-space comparison E*(CP∞)≃E*[[x]] is completed in the skeletal topology. Tensor product of line bundles defines a graded commutative one-dimensional formal group law F_E. For even-periodic E choose an invertible degree-two class to obtain a degree-zero coordinate and an actual Mathlib FormalGroup over π₀E.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use oriented finite projective spaces and their cell filtrations to prove the compatible power-series description.
Pull the orientation back along tensor product, then read the formal group identities from tensor-product associativity, symmetry and identity.
Coordinate changes are formal isomorphisms imported from LT.0, with the prescribed derivative.
acceptance: HZ with its standard orientation gives the additive law.
KU with the degree-zero coordinate [L]−1 gives X+Y+XY.
Changing coordinate does not change the geometric height; a random power series with nonunit linear term is not an orientation coordinate.

nodes.title: Geometric height of an orientation
nodes.statement: For a commutative one-dimensional law over a characteristic-p field, its canonical continuous Z_p-action makes it an instance of the LT.0 formal-module notion: [p]_F has initial nonzero degree p^h, or is zero and has height ∞. Assign height zero where p is invertible. For an even-periodic p-local oriented ring E, geometric height at most n means this bound at every geometric point of Spec π₀E, with the orientation expressed in a degree-zero coordinate. For a general graded orientation, the sufficient uniform bound used here is the explicit condition (p,v₁,…,v_n)=π_*E on the invariant p-typical coefficient ideal. Coordinate change preserves these conditions.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Extend integer multiplication on a characteristic-p law to Z_p: differences divisible by p^r have order tending to infinity unless [p]=0, when they already vanish.
Use LT.0’s height invariant and its change-of-coordinate theorem.
Apply the condition at geometric points; keep residue-characteristic-zero points separate.
acceptance: Over F_p, the additive law has infinite height since [p]=0.
Over F_p, the multiplicative law has [p](X)=X^p and height one.
An ordinary elliptic formal group has height one and a supersingular elliptic formal group has height two; neither height is assigned to an arbitrary law merely because it has dimension one.

nodes.title: Morava K-theory and Johnson–Wilson spectra
nodes.statement: For n≥1 construct BP⟨n⟩ and k(n) as BP-module quotients with π_*BP⟨n⟩=Z_(p)[v₁,…,v_n] and π_*k(n)=F_p[v_n]. Form E(n)=BP⟨n⟩[v_n⁻¹] and K(n)=k(n)[v_n⁻¹], with graded coefficients Z_(p)[v₁,…,v_(n−1),v_n^±1] and F_p[v_n^±1]. Set BP⟨0⟩=k(0)=HZ_(p), E(0)=K(0)=HQ, and K(∞)=HF_p. K(n) admits a unital homotopy-associative multiplication; no homotopy commutativity at p=2 or E∞ quotient structure is imposed.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Construct module quotients by regular coefficient sequences and choose compatible v_n actions.
Invert the action by the sequential homotopy colimit, computing homotopy groups using the supplier’s telescope formula.
Supply the ring structures needed for nilpotence detection separately from module quotient existence.
acceptance: K(0) has Q in degree zero and no other homotopy groups.
For n≥1, K(n)_* is a graded field with a nonzero class precisely in degrees divisible by 2(p^n−1).
K(∞)=HF_p is distinct from every periodic K(n).

nodes.title: Connective periodic cofiber sequences
nodes.statement: For n≥1 there are BP-module cofiber sequences Σ^(2p^n−2)BP⟨n⟩→BP⟨n⟩→BP⟨n−1⟩ and Σ^(2p^n−2)k(n)→k(n)→HF_p, with first maps multiplication by v_n. Multiplication by p on BP⟨0⟩=HZ_(p) has cofiber HF_p. Inverting v_n in the first two middle terms gives E(n) and K(n). For every spectrum X, K(n)_*(X⊗Y)≅K(n)_*X⊗_(K(n)_*)K(n)_*Y; in particular K(m)⊗K(n)=0 for m≠n, including the stated endpoints 0 and ∞. For finite V, duality preserves vanishing of K(n)-homology.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use regularity of the coefficient element and the homotopy exact sequence to identify quotient modules.
For Künneth, split K(n)-modules into wedges of suspensions of K(n) by choosing homogeneous bases; use this only as a graded-field argument.
The different-height vanishing uses the chosen p-typical v_n action on each coefficient theory.
Apply finite duality after base change to the graded-field K(n)-module category; a finite graded vector space vanishes exactly when its dual does.
acceptance: At n=1 the quotient of BP⟨1⟩ by v₁ is HZ_(p), whereas the quotient of k(1) is HF_p.

nodes.title: Chromatic type
nodes.statement: For n≥0 let C_n⊂FinSp_(p) consist of V with K(i)⊗V=0 for all 0≤i<n. A nonzero V has type n if V∈C_n and K(n)⊗V≠0; the zero object alone has type ∞. Each C_n is a thick tensor ideal. C_0 is all finite p-local spectra; C_1 is the finite rationally acyclic subcategory.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: K(n)-homology is exact, so the vanishing conditions are closed under shifts, finite cofibers and retracts. The graded-field Künneth theorem gives the tensor-ideal property.

For a nonzero finite p-local spectrum, mod-p homology is nonzero. Lemma 2.1 compares it, degree by degree in the finite cell range, with K(n)-homology for sufficiently large n; thus a first nonvanishing finite height exists. This argument does not assume the thick-subcategory classification.

The nested-support statement identifies the customary single-detector definition with vanishing at all smaller heights. Künneth then gives type(V⊗W)=max(type V,type W), with the zero-object convention.
acceptance: S_(p) has type zero.
S/p has type one.
The zero spectrum is in every C_n and must not be assigned any finite exact type.

nodes.title: Nilpotence theorem
nodes.statement: A map f:V→X with V finite is smash nilpotent if and only if K(i)_*f=0 for every i∈{0,1,2,…,∞}. A self-map of a finite spectrum is nilpotent under composition if and only if its action on every K(i)-homology is nilpotent. For an associative unital ring spectrum R and x∈π_*R, x is nilpotent if and only if its image in K(i)_*R is nilpotent for every i, including K(∞)=HF_p. State the integral version by varying the prime; here V and rings are p-local where the fixed-prime formulation is used. For the particular unit-detection consequence for p-local R, namely R=0 iff all K(i)⊗R=0, a unital magma in the homotopy category suffices; associativity is retained for the general graded-element formulation.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.

nodes.title: Fiberwise homology comparison
nodes.statement: Let f:X→Y be a map of spaces and E a spectrum. If for every y the augmentation E⊗Σ∞_+fib_y(f)→E is an equivalence, then E⊗Σ∞_+f is an equivalence, with no finiteness hypothesis on Y and no boundedness hypothesis on E. For pointed connected fibers the hypothesis says that their reduced E-homology vanishes. This theorem supplies the arbitrary-base comparison even when a periodic Serre spectral sequence has no established strong convergence.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Unstraighten f as a space-indexed local system of spaces; after applying E⊗Σ∞_+ its colimit over Y is E⊗Σ∞_+X.
The fiber augmentations give a natural equivalence to the constant local system E.

Take colimits. Compose the left Kan extension along f with that along Y→*; its pointwise fiber formula identifies the first colimit with E⊗Σ∞_+X and the constant-system colimit with E⊗Σ∞_+Y. The unstraightening and space-indexed Fubini comparison are explicit parts of the E3 request.
acceptance: It applies to Y infinite and E periodic.
The augmentation condition uses unreduced fibers; asserting E_*(F_+)=0 would incorrectly fail even for a point.

nodes.title: Connective periodic vanishing
nodes.statement: For every n≥1 there is an integer m≥2 such that an m-connective pointed space whose v_i-periodic homotopy groups vanish for 0≤i≤n is L_n^(p,f)-acyclic after reduced suspension spectrum. Consequently an m-connective map of spaces which is a v_i-periodic equivalence for all 0≤i≤n induces an L_n^(p,f)-equivalence on suspension spectra. One can take m=n+1 using the Carmeli–Schlank–Yanovski height bound; keep this sharpened bound separate from Bousfield’s original dimension-dependent bound.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use Bousfield’s finite-nullification comparison: sufficiently connected periodic equivalences are equivalences after nullification at a type-(n+1) finite complex.
Identify stable acyclicity by mapping into Ω∞ of finite-local spectra as in Barthel–Heuts–Meier Lemma 3.3.
For the sharper bound use CSY Theorem 5.4.4 and Remark 5.4.5, then the fiberwise comparison. The precise nullification theorem and the CSY categorical-height argument are recorded as G5.

No claim is made for arbitrary disconnected fibers.

nodes.title: Morava E-theory
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and G a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height h≥1 over k. Import its marked universal deformation ring R(k,G), noncanonically W(k)[[u₁,…,u_(h−1)]]. Construct a K(h)-local even-periodic E∞ ring E(k,G) with π₀E=R(k,G), π_*E≅R(k,G)[u^±1], |u|=−2, and formal group the universal deformation of G. The realization space equipped with that deformation identification is contractible. The coefficient isomorphism and coordinate are choices, not canonical identifications.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Import marked deformation representability with B=W(k), not a new deformation functor.
Apply Landweber realization to the universal law and the Goerss–Hopkins–Miller realization theorem to obtain the coherent E∞ refinement and contractible realization space.
The obstruction-theoretic construction of this refinement is G9; ordinary representability alone gives no E∞ structure.
acceptance: For h=1 and k=F_p the deformation ring is Z_p, with no deformation parameters.
For h=2 and k=F_(p²), π₀ is W(F_(p²))[[u₁]].
A height-∞ law is outside this finite-height realization theorem.

sources.match: The local Hopkins–Miller theorem realizes the finite-height universal deformation.

nodes.title: Morava stabilizer actions
nodes.statement: Make E(k,G) functorial on the groupoid of perfect characteristic-p fields with specified isomorphisms of their height-h formal groups after coefficient transport. Aut(k,G) acts coherently through E∞ maps. For a Honda law over F_(p^h), specify the extended stabilizer G_h=Aut(G/F_(p^h))⋊Gal(F_(p^h)/F_p). Its action on coefficients is continuous for the maximal-ideal topology, and its finite subgroup restrictions are coherent finite actions usable in Tate and homotopy fixed points. A profinite action is not modeled as a discrete finite-quotient action on E_h.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use functoriality of the marked deformation groupoid, followed by the functorial Goerss–Hopkins–Miller realization.
Compare coefficient automorphisms with the algebraic stabilizer action; reduce modulo successive powers of the maximal ideal to express continuity.
Restrict to actual finite subgroups for the finite-action API. Continuous homotopy fixed points for arbitrary closed subgroups are outside the targets; no Devinatz–Hopkins descent is silently used.

nodes.title: Ravenel’s Bousfield class formula
nodes.statement: For n≥0, ⟨BP[v_n⁻¹]⟩=⟨E(n)⟩=⟨K(0)∨⋯∨K(n)⟩, with v₀=p. Moreover ⟨BP⟨n⟩⟩=⟨E(n)∨HF_p⟩ and ⟨k(n)⟩=⟨K(n)∨HF_p⟩ for n≥1. The formulas are statements of Bousfield classes, not equivalences of spectra.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use the BP quotient/localization sequences to separate consecutive heights.
Apply the regular-invariant-ideal base-change comparison and the distributive Bousfield-class calculation in Ravenel Theorem 2.1.
The regular-sequence realization and Landweber comparison are recorded in G6; algebraic coefficient identities alone do not prove the Bousfield equalities.

nodes.title: Finite-height locality
nodes.statement: Let R be a p-local even-periodic oriented homotopy commutative ring with geometric height at most n at every point of Spec π₀R. Then R and every R-module are L_n-local. The graded variant assumes the explicit unit-ideal criterion (p,v₁,…,v_n)=π_*R. The pointwise condition in the even-periodic case implies that criterion after converting the coefficients to degree zero. These statements require a uniform finite bound; no bound is inferred merely from having a one-dimensional law.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Apply p-typicalization. Over π₀R the height condition makes the ideal of the degree-zero forms of p,v₁,…,v_n the unit ideal.

Each principal-open term is a unital module, at least in the homotopy category, over the relevant inverted BP ring. Its Bousfield class is bounded by E(n). For an E(n)-acyclic A, the free/cofree adjunction or the unital retract M→F(BP[v_i⁻¹],M)→M forces Map(A,M) to vanish. Thus the module is local; the conclusion is not inferred from a bound on the module’s Bousfield class alone.
The finite Čech diagram reconstructs R and each R-module. Local objects are closed under limits. Apply the same invariant-ideal argument in the graded variant; G6 records its proof-level comparison.
acceptance: An even-periodic elliptic theory has bound two.
The additive characteristic-p theory has infinite height and does not meet a finite bound.

sources.match: A uniformly bounded complex-oriented height forces chromatic locality.
The height-at-most-n locus corresponds to E(n)-localization.

nodes.title: Hopkins–Ravenel smashing theorem
nodes.statement: For every n≥0, L_nX≃L_nS⊗X naturally, compatibly with the localization unit. In the L_n-local category, E_n generates the unit as a thick tensor ideal: the E_n-based cobar totalization tower is pro-constant with value L_nS. Here E_n is Morava E-theory at height n≥1; treat height zero rationally. The pro-constant statement has uniform finite-stage retraction content, stronger than mere convergence of a spectral sequence.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use the horizontal vanishing line in the E_n-local Adams–Novikov spectral sequence and Bousfield’s pro-constancy criterion.
A finite partial totalization then has the unit as a retract, making E_n descendable in the L_n-local category.
The horizontal vanishing and its construction are G7; no smashing conclusion is inferred just from the Bousfield-class definition.
acceptance: The theorem is for L_n; it does not assert that L_(K(n)) is smashing on all spectra.
A convergent tower need not be pro-constant, so convergence alone is insufficient.

sources.match: The uniform vanishing line and pro-constant cobar tower supply the strong smash-product input.

nodes.title: Telescopes on chromatically local spectra
nodes.statement: For n≥1, every L_(n−1)-local spectrum is T(n)-acyclic. For every L_n-local X, the canonical comparison L_(T(n))X→L_(K(n))X is an equivalence. Both assertions require the stated chromatic locality and do not prove equality of the two localization functors on all spectra. The p-local chromatic level one agrees with KU_(p)-localization; globally L_KU detects all primes rather than a fixed-p tower.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: By Hopkins–Ravenel smashing, every L_(n−1)-local X is L_(n−1)S⊗X. Ravenel orthogonality makes the ring L_(n−1)S K(n)-acyclic; ring acyclicity then makes it T(n)-acyclic, and smashing with X proves the first assertion. This uses the ring comparison on the localized sphere, not on an arbitrary module.
Apply the chromatic fracture square to L_n-local X; its lower piece is T(n)-acyclic and its height-n piece is detected by K(n).
At height one compare the p-local KU Bousfield class with E(1) and HQ∨K(1), importing complex Bott theory. The telescope comparison on L_n-local objects is included in G7 for proof expansion.
acceptance: KU_(p) is L₁-local, but its p-completion must still be distinguished from global KU.
An arbitrary T(n)-local spectrum at n≥2 need not be K(n)-local.

nodes.title: Separation above height one
nodes.statement: At height one and every prime, the Bousfield classes of T(1) and K(1) agree. At every prime and every height n≥2, there exists a T(n)-local spectrum which is not K(n)-local. Thus a general-spectrum identification of the two theories is false. This node records the exact boundary on all comparisons; its higher-height proof uses algebraic K-theory and is a separately recorded gap, not a prerequisite of the ring acyclicity theorem.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: For height one use the localized Adams computations of Miller at odd primes and Mahowald at two, quoted in BHLS.
For higher height use BHLS Theorem A with its T(n)-localized K-theory counterexample; its K-theoretic construction and cyclotomic non-hyperdescent proof are G8.
No counterexample object is defined here by an arbitrary spectrum or a formal axiom.
acceptance: The equality at height one is not described as an open conjecture.
The higher-height failure does not contradict the acyclicity criterion for unital rings.

sources.match: The theorem separates the local categories at every prime and every height at least two; the introduction recalls the height-one theorem.

nodes.title: Chromatic support of BP truncations
nodes.statement: For n≥0 and i>n, BP⟨n⟩ is K(i)-acyclic and T(i)-acyclic. For n≥1 the map BP⟨n⟩→E(n) is a T(n)-equivalence, and is also a T(i)-equivalence for i>n because both objects are acyclic there. It is not an L_n^f-equivalence in general: the rational homotopy of BP⟨n⟩ is connective, whereas E(n) has negative rational classes for n≥1.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Smash Ravenel’s class formula ⟨BP⟨n⟩⟩=⟨E(n)∨HF_p⟩ with T(i), i>n. The class of E(n) is the join of K(0),…,K(n), and each of those, as well as HF_p, annihilates T(i) by telescope orthogonality. This proves the T(i)-vanishing without choosing a ring structure on BP⟨n⟩; the K(i)-vanishing follows from the same class formula.
The successive v_n-cofibers are shifts of BP⟨n−1⟩. They are T(n)-acyclic, so the sequential inversion map is a T(n)-equivalence.
At n=1, rationalization preserves the distinction between the connective polynomial coefficient ring and its Laurent localization, disproving the stronger routed assertion.
acceptance: For n=1 the inversion map is a T(1)-equivalence but fails to be a rational equivalence.
For n=0, BP⟨0⟩=HZ_(p) has no positive finite-height support.

sources.match: The truncation and inverted-theory Bousfield classes give the asserted support.

nodes.title: Localized norms and Tate spectra
nodes.statement: Import coherent finite-group orbits, fixed points, the normalized norm, its Tate cofiber, and the lax symmetric monoidal Tate functor from RefinedTraceMethods RT.2. For an E-local spectrum X with coherent G-action, the norm in Sp_E is L_E(X_hG)→X^hG, and its cofiber is L_E(X^tG). The fixed points are already E-local because local objects are closed under limits. The imported Tate module structure is compatible with this comparison. This node owns only the passage to the homological localization.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Compute colimits in Sp_E by applying L_E to ambient colimits, and limits by the fully faithful inclusion.
Apply the exact functor L_E to the imported norm cofiber sequence; identify its target with X^hG.

nodes.statement: For a homological localization L and finite G, these are equivalent: every G-object in LSp has norm equivalence; L((LS)^tG)=0 for the trivial action on LS; the transfer Σ∞_+BG→S admits a section after L. If these properties hold for prime-order groups they hold for every finite group. The transfer Σ∞_+BC_p→S admits a section after Ω^(∞+1), by Kahn–Priddy in its cyclic-group form.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Reduce arbitrary X to the Tate algebra of the local sphere via its module structure.
A transfer section produces an element whose norm restricts to 1 at the basepoint; the unit criterion in multiplicative cohomology of connected spaces makes it a unit.

nodes.title: Morava power operations
nodes.statement: For height-(h+1) Morava E-theory E with π₀E=W(F_(p^(h+1)))[[u₁,…,u_h]] and a K(h+1)-local E∞ E-algebra R, construct the weight-p operation P:π₀R→R⁰(BC_p). It is multiplicative and unital, and becomes additive after quotienting by the transfer. The transfer generator in E⁰(BC_p)=E₀[[z]]/([p](z)) is [p](z)/z. For 1≤k<h, after reducing by I_(k+1)=(p,u₁,…,u_k), define g_(k+1) by [p](z)=z^(p^(k+1))g_(k+1)(z). If x maps to zero in π₀ of the iterated module quotient R/(p,u₁,…,u_k), then P(x) maps to zero in π₀ of R^BC_p/(p,u₁,…,u_k,g_(k+1)). These are module cofibers; no identification with ordinary ring quotients for arbitrary R is assumed. For R=E the regular coefficient case gives the quotient ring operation used in the valuation calculation. The k=0 Bockstein case is an explicit part of G14, rather than attributed to the printed k≥1 theorem.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Apply the E∞ multiplication to extended p-th powers and the diagonal class.
Identify the transfer ideal using the complex orientation and the p-series.

Apply Hahn Theorem 3.3 to iterated module cofibers. Its Bockstein power admits an equivariant section after the specified g quotient; hence zero classes have zero image. Specialize to E for the regular coefficient ring operation. The k=0 extension is retained separately in G14.
acceptance: P(1)=1 and P(xy)=P(x)P(y).
Additivity is required only after quotienting by the transfer, so P(x+y)=P(x)+P(y) is not imposed in the original target.
The quotient [p](z)/z^(p^(k+1)) is formed only after reducing by I_(k+1), not as an integral power series in the original ring.

nodes.title: Hahn’s acyclicity theorem
nodes.statement: For an E∞ ring spectrum R and h≥0, K(h)⊗R=0 implies K(h+1)⊗R=0. Consequently T(h)⊗R=0 implies T(h+1)⊗R=0 for h≥0, with T(0)=S[1/p]. For h≥1 translate by the ring-spectrum comparison; at h=0 use S[1/p]-acyclicity⇒HQ-acyclicity, not the false equality of these acyclic classes on all spectra.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.

nodes.statement: Let (S³)_p^∧ be the p-completion of the nilpotent space S³ and let f_p:Ω²(S³)_p^∧→BGL₁(S_p^∧) be the E₂ map extending the class 1−p∈π₁BGL₁(S_p^∧)=Z_p^× in the p-complete convention. Its p-complete Thom E₂ ring is HF_p. Set C_p=fib((S³)_p^∧→K(Z_p,3)), with the map inducing the identity on π₃. Restriction along Ω²C_p gives the p-complete Thom E₂ ring HZ_p. Here C_p is the 3-connected cover; using an uncompleted S³ with target K(Z_p,3) would give π₂=Z_p/Z instead. Thom tensor products and colimits in these assertions are taken in the p-complete symmetric monoidal category.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: Use H.6’s spectral p-completion and CH.0’s homological localization to identify p-complete spectra with Sp_(S/p), whose tensor and colimits are completed. Model the nilpotent source-space completion and compare its connected cover with the completion of fib(S³→K(Z,3)); this comparison is included in G19.
Identify the Thom E₂ ring with the versal E₂ ring killing p via the universal property.
Compute its mod-p homology and the Dyer–Lashof operations to identify the map to HF_p.
For the integral connected-cover variant use the intermediate Thom construction over S¹ and its characteristic-p quotient. The free E₂ homology and operation computation is G19.
acceptance: At p=2 the selected unit is −1.
The HF_p Thom ring has π₀=F_p, while the connected-cover integral variant has π₀=Z_p.
The completed-source cover C_p has π_i=0 for i≤3. The fiber of the uncompleted-domain map S³→K(Z_p,3) fails this check in degree two.

nodes.title: James-filtered Thom spectra
nodes.statement: For m≥0 restrict f_p along ΩJ_(p^m−1)S²→Ω²S³→Ω²(S³)_p^∧ and denote the resulting p-complete E₁ Thom ring by y(m). All colimits in this family are colimits in p-complete spectra, formed by completing ordinary spectral colimits. Then y(0)=S_p^∧, there are E₁ maps y(m)→y(m+1), and colim_m y(m)≃HF_p. For m≥1, π₀y(m)=F_p. At p=2 and m≥1 define z(m) by restricting along Ω(J_(2^m−1)S²⟨2⟩), where the inner connected cover is the fiber of J_(2^m−1)S²→K(Z,2), followed by completion in the p-complete convention. These E₁ rings map to y(m), and colim z(m)≃HZ₂.

hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
proofSteps: At height zero use the F_p-valued π₀ of the connective ring y(m), which makes all its homotopy groups p-torsion.

At odd primes compare the Adams vanishing-line slope 1/(2p^m−2) with a v_i action of reciprocal slope 1/|v_i| for i<m, forcing v_i-torsion after localization. The convergence and slope proof are G20.
For z(m), keep the integral degree-zero class and the positive-height range exactly.

hypotheses: Fix a prime p; spectra and tensor products are derived.
